title: Messages, tasks and artifacts
brief: A remote agent gets a request that may be a quick answer, a long job or a conversation. How it models the reply, the state and the follow-ups decides whether callers can reason about the work. Choose a response style and learn the rules that keep ids and states consistent.

blocks.caption: Core objects in the v1.0 spec [[r1]]
head: Object
Key fields
Rules worth knowing
rows: The server generates `id`. It is the stateful unit of work with a lifecycle
Roles are `ROLE_USER` and `ROLE_AGENT`. If both ids are given they must match, and with only `taskId` the server infers the context
`raw` is base64 in JSON. The v0.3 `kind` discriminator is gone
A task output. `artifactId` is unique within the task and at least one part is required

blocks.title: Typical task lifecycle
blocks.alt: A task is submitted and then working. It can pause in input required or auth required and return to working. It ends in completed, failed, canceled or rejected.
blocks.src:
stateDiagram-v2
  [*] --> SUBMITTED
  SUBMITTED --> WORKING
  SUBMITTED --> REJECTED
  WORKING --> INPUT_REQUIRED
  INPUT_REQUIRED --> WORKING: client replies
  WORKING --> AUTH_REQUIRED
  AUTH_REQUIRED --> WORKING: credential obtained
  WORKING --> COMPLETED
  WORKING --> FAILED
  WORKING --> CANCELED
  COMPLETED --> [*]
blocks.caption: State names carry the prefix `TASK_STATE_` on the wire. Terminal: COMPLETED, FAILED, CANCELED, REJECTED. Interrupted: INPUT_REQUIRED and AUTH_REQUIRED. The spec defines the states and says terminal tasks accept no more messages. It does not publish a strict transition table, so treat the arrows as the usual flow [[r1]].

blocks.title: How should an agent respond to a message?
blocks.intro: Three styles from the Life of a Task guide [[r5]].

options.name: Message-only agent
options.summary: Always answer with a Message and use `contextId` to tie turns together.
cons: No progress tracking or interrupted states
options.bestWhen: The agent wraps a quick LLM call or simple tools.
options.avoidWhen: Work is long-running or needs input-required handling.

options.name: Task-generating agent
options.summary: Always return a Task, even for a plain answer, which becomes a completed task.
pros: Every unit of work is trackable and attributable
cons: Completed task objects for trivial exchanges
Once a task exists, later replies are tasks too
options.bestWhen: You need an audit trail and retries per request.

options.name: Hybrid agent
options.summary: Use Messages to agree on scope, then create a Task for committed work.
pros: Task tracking only where it pays
cons: Callers must handle both result shapes
options.bestWhen: Scope needs a short dialogue before a long job.
options.avoidWhen: A tiny agent with one fixed behavior.

blocks.title: A multi-turn exchange, end to end

steps.title: Send
steps.md: Client calls `SendMessage` with a message and no ids.

steps.title: Task
steps.md: Agent returns a Task with a server-made `taskId` and `contextId`.

steps.title: Ask
steps.md: State becomes `INPUT_REQUIRED` with a status message.

steps.title: Reply
steps.md: Client sends the same `taskId` and `contextId` with its answer.

steps.title: Refine
steps.md: A new message with the same `contextId` and `referenceTaskIds` starts a new task.

blocks.title: Failure modes and how to detect them

items.cause: The client sent a message to a task in a terminal state. Terminal tasks cannot restart
items.fix: Start a new task in the same `contextId` and set `referenceTaskIds`. Detect it by counting errors on terminal tasks

items.symptom: An answer to a clarification starts a fresh task
items.cause: The reply carried only `contextId`. A `contextId` without `taskId` starts a new task in that conversation
items.fix: Include the original `taskId` as well as `contextId` when resuming

items.symptom: Requests with client-made ids are rejected
items.cause: Clients cannot create tasks with their own `taskId`, and a `contextId` that does not match the task is rejected
items.fix: Let the server generate ids, treat `contextId` as opaque and echo ids unchanged

items.symptom: Users see tasks that belong to someone else
items.cause: `GetTask` or `ListTasks` was not scoped to the authenticated caller
items.fix: Check authorization before any query. Return `TaskNotFoundError` for tasks the caller cannot access [[r1]]

items.symptom: A caller shows an outdated report after a refinement
items.cause: Refinements create new artifacts and the protocol does not track versions
items.fix: Clients keep a version history. Agents reuse a consistent artifact name for refined versions [[r5]]

items.title: Operations and where they live on the wire

blocks.md: `ListTasks` uses cursor pagination and is scoped to the caller. Cancellation is idempotent. A duplicate cancel MAY return `TaskNotFoundError` if the task was already canceled and purged [[r1]].

items: `TaskNotFoundError`: the id does not exist or is not accessible
`TaskNotCancelableError`: the task is not in a cancelable state
`UnsupportedOperationError`: terminal task, or streaming or the extended card is not supported
`PushNotificationNotSupportedError`: push is not declared in the card
`ContentTypeNotSupportedError`: a part's media type is not accepted
`ExtensionSupportRequiredError` and `VersionNotSupportedError`: a required extension or the requested version is missing

quiz.q: Put a typical multi-turn A2A exchange in order.
items: Client sends `SendMessage` with a message and no ids
Agent returns a Task with server-generated `taskId` and `contextId`
Task moves to `INPUT_REQUIRED` and carries a question
Client replies with the same `taskId` and `contextId`
quiz.explain: Clients cannot supply a new `taskId`, so the server mints ids on the first response. The question pauses the task in an interrupted state. The resume must reuse both ids. Completion produces the artifact.

quiz.q: The client log is shown. What is the correct fix?

code.code:
t=0   SendMessage -> Task id=t-77 contextId=c-1 state=TASK_STATE_COMPLETED
t=90  SendMessage taskId=t-77 contextId=c-1 "add a summary" -> UnsupportedOperationError

options: Retry the same call after a short delay, because the agent was briefly unavailable and a terminal state clears itself after some minutes of inactivity
Send the follow-up as a new message in `contextId` c-1 and reference `t-77` in `referenceTaskIds`, so the agent creates a new task
Remove `contextId` so the server accepts the old `taskId`
Generate a fresh `taskId` on the client for the follow-up
quiz.explain: `COMPLETED` is terminal and terminal tasks cannot accept messages or restart. A refinement is a new task in the same context. Retrying cannot help, removing `contextId` does not reopen the task, and clients cannot create their own task ids.

quiz.q: Match each A2A object or state to its role.

pairs.r: The stateful unit of work with a lifecycle
Exactly one of text, raw bytes, a URL or structured data
An interrupted state that waits for the client
A terminal state where the agent decided not to perform the task

quiz.explain: A Task carries status, artifacts and history. A Part is a union of four content forms. Input-required is interrupted, not terminal. Rejected is terminal and means the agent declined the work.

takeaways: The server mints `taskId` and `contextId`. Clients echo them. A `contextId` without a `taskId` starts a new task.
Terminal tasks are immutable. Refinements start new tasks in the same context and reference earlier ones.
Choose message-only, task-generating or hybrid by whether work is long-running and needs tracking.
Scope every task operation to the authenticated caller and return `TaskNotFoundError` for anything else.
